use: Wall units both cool and heat, so it's on in winter too.

example.ja: 暑いからエアコンつけて
example.english: It's hot, turn on the air con.

examplePolite.romaji: atsui node eakon o tsukete kudasai
examplePolite.ja: 暑いのでエアコンをつけてください
examplePolite.english: It's hot, so please turn on the air conditioning.

notes: Tsukeru turns it on, kesu turns it off.

use: Short for denshi renji; it means the microwave, not a stove.

example.romaji: sore renji de atatamereba ii yo
example.ja: それレンジで温めればいいよ
example.english: Just heat it up in the microwave.

examplePolite.romaji: sore wa renji de atatamereba ii desu yo
examplePolite.ja: それはレンジで温めればいいですよ
examplePolite.english: You can just heat that in the microwave.

notes: Chin suru is a casual way to say microwave something.

example.ja: テレビのリモコンどこ行った?
example.english: Where'd the TV remote go?

examplePolite.romaji: terebi no rimokon wa doko desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: テレビのリモコンはどこですか?
examplePolite.english: Where's the TV remote?

use: To vacuum is soujiki o kakeru.

example.ja: 部屋に掃除機かけといたよ
example.english: I vacuumed the room.

examplePolite.romaji: heya ni soujiki o kakete okimashita
examplePolite.ja: 部屋に掃除機をかけておきました
examplePolite.english: I've vacuumed the room.

notes: Souji is cleaning; soujiki is the machine.

example.romaji: ryouri kekkou tokui na n da
example.ja: 料理けっこう得意なんだ
example.english: I'm actually pretty good at cooking.

examplePolite.romaji: ryouri wa kekkou tokui na n desu
examplePolite.ja: 料理はけっこう得意なんです
examplePolite.english: I'm actually quite good at cooking.

notes: Ryouri suru means to cook. As cuisine: nihon ryouri is Japanese food.

use: Mostly as hamigaki suru, to brush your teeth.

example.ja: 寝る前に歯磨きした?
example.english: Did you brush your teeth before bed?

examplePolite.romaji: neru mae ni hamigaki shimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 寝る前に歯磨きしましたか?
examplePolite.english: Did you brush your teeth before going to bed?

use: Usually dirty dishes; goes with suru or yaru.

example.romaji: araimono wa ato de yattoku ne
example.ja: 洗い物はあとでやっとくね
example.english: I'll do the dishes later.

examplePolite.romaji: araimono wa ato de yatte okimasu
examplePolite.ja: 洗い物はあとでやっておきます
examplePolite.english: I'll take care of the dishes later.

notes: Can also mean laundry waiting to be washed.

use: Courier delivery to your door; you hear 'takuhaibin desu' at the intercom.

example.ja: さっき宅配便来てたよ
example.english: A parcel came for you earlier.

examplePolite.romaji: sakki takuhaibin ga kite imashita yo
examplePolite.ja: さっき宅配便が来ていましたよ
examplePolite.english: A delivery came earlier.

notes: Takkyuubin is heard for the same thing.

english: cook for yourself; make your own meals
use: Said of people living alone who cook instead of eating out or buying ready meals.

example.romaji: hitorigurashi da kedo mainichi jisui shiteru yo
example.ja: 一人暮らしだけど毎日自炊してるよ
example.english: I live alone, but I cook for myself every day.

examplePolite.romaji: hitorigurashi desu ga mainichi jisui shite imasu
examplePolite.ja: 一人暮らしですが毎日自炊しています
examplePolite.english: I live alone, but I cook my own meals every day.

use: Home-made or bought at a convenience store; usually said obentou.

example.ja: 今日お弁当持ってきた?
example.english: Did you bring a lunch today?

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa obentou o motte kimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今日はお弁当を持ってきましたか?
examplePolite.english: Did you bring a packed lunch today?

notes: Convenience store staff ask 'atatamemasu ka?': do you want it heated?

use: Most often the shared hot-pot meal cooked at the table in winter.

example.romaji: samui shi kon'ya wa nabe ni shiyou yo
example.ja: 寒いし今夜は鍋にしようよ
example.english: It's cold, let's have hot pot tonight.

examplePolite.romaji: samui node kon'ya wa nabe ni shimashou
examplePolite.ja: 寒いので今夜は鍋にしましょう
examplePolite.english: It's cold, so let's have hot pot tonight.

notes: Also the cooking pot or saucepan itself.

example.romaji: konbini de onigiri katte kuru ne
example.ja: コンビニでおにぎり買ってくるね
example.english: I'll go grab some rice balls from the convenience store.

examplePolite.romaji: konbini de onigiri o katte kimasu ne
examplePolite.ja: コンビニでおにぎりを買ってきますね
examplePolite.english: I'll go and buy some rice balls at the convenience store.

notes: Also called omusubi in some places.

example.ja: 味噌汁飲むとほっとする
example.english: Miso soup always makes me feel at home.

examplePolite.romaji: misoshiru o nomu to hotto shimasu
examplePolite.ja: 味噌汁を飲むとほっとします
examplePolite.english: Drinking miso soup makes me relax.

notes: Often said omisoshiru. You drink it from the bowl, so the verb is nomu.

example.ja: メニュー見てから決めよう
example.english: Let's look at the menu and then decide.

examplePolite.romaji: menyuu o mite kara kimemashou
examplePolite.ja: メニューを見てから決めましょう
examplePolite.english: Let's decide after looking at the menu.

notes: Also a list of options outside food, like a workout menu.

use: Mostly for lunch out; lunch at home is hirugohan.

example.ja: 明日一緒にランチ行かない?
example.english: Want to go to lunch together tomorrow?

examplePolite.romaji: ashita issho ni ranchi ni ikimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 明日一緒にランチに行きませんか?
examplePolite.english: Would you like to have lunch together tomorrow?

notes: Restaurants offer cheap ranchi sets at midday.

use: Talks about the habit of eating out rather than one restaurant meal.

example.ja: 最近外食ばっかりだな
example.english: I've been eating out way too much lately.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin gaishoku bakari desu
examplePolite.ja: 最近外食ばかりです
examplePolite.english: Lately I've been eating out all the time.

notes: Gaishoku suru means eat out. The opposite is jisui (cooking for yourself).

use: A set price, usually with a time limit.

example.ja: 焼肉の食べ放題行こうよ
example.english: Let's go to an all-you-can-eat barbecue place.

examplePolite.romaji: yakiniku no tabehoudai ni ikimashou
examplePolite.ja: 焼肉の食べ放題に行きましょう
examplePolite.english: Let's go for all-you-can-eat barbecue.

use: Staff ask 'omochikaeri desu ka?': is it to go?

example.ja: 混んでるし持ち帰りにしない?
example.english: It's packed, want to get it to go?

examplePolite.romaji: konde iru node mochikaeri ni shimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 混んでいるので持ち帰りにしませんか?
examplePolite.english: It's crowded, so shall we get it to go?

notes: Eating in is tennai or kochira de. Teikuauto is also used.

example.ja: 同じチームで頑張ろう
example.english: We're on the same team, let's give it our all.

examplePolite.romaji: onaji chiimu de ganbarimashou
examplePolite.ja: 同じチームで頑張りましょう
examplePolite.english: Let's do our best together on the same team.

use: Where the hands-on work happens, like a building site, film set or shop floor.

example.ja: 今から現場行ってくる
example.english: I'm heading out to the site now.

examplePolite.romaji: ima kara genba ni itte kimasu
examplePolite.ja: 今から現場に行ってきます
examplePolite.english: I'm going out to the site now.

notes: In crime dramas it's the crime or accident scene.
